task_title: Make Floor 1 AI tasks scenario-config driven

plan_review.notes: Adopted the quest-derived graph plus scenario adapter alternative. Quest pack IDs/objectives remain canonical and a validated Floor 1 AI overlay supplies only runtime dependencies/effects, generic operations, eligibility/completion, work estimation, and execution. Rejected a duplicated full-chain config due to drift; rejected registry-local callbacks due to scenarioDefinitions bloat; rejected Floor-1-shaped target kinds in favor of generic move/interact/engage/farm/ambient operations. Revised plan includes explicit negative door effects, deterministic snapshot/revision keys, committed-task reverse mapping, load-time graph validation, and migration of auto-progression consumers.

independent_grade.notes: The refactor extracts Floor 1's imperative goal-graph builder into a generic chain/anchor interpreter plus a scenario-owned overlay, and the semantic mapping is faithful. I verified the delicate cases: (a) initialSatisfiedEffects seeding — every old top-level `if` block (`questCompleted`, `bossBattleAccepted||slimeRatStarted`, `slimeRatDefeated`, `bossBattleComplete`, `staircaseDefeated`, `shopStage==='complete'`) is reproduced by a matching task's `satisfiedInitially` + `unlockEffects` pair; (b) chain-anchor prerequisites reproduce the old `preChainTail`/`shopTail`/`spellTail` tail-hopping, including the empty-tail fallback that made `staircaseGate` empty when a chain contributed nothing; (c) the dynamic `take-stairs` prereq (kill / finish / staircaseGate) falls out naturally from the chain because kill-* and finish-* are mutually exclusive on `slimeRatStarted`/`staircaseStarted`; (d) the dispatch switch in `bt-ai-provider.ts` reproduces each old case's `createProgressTarget` arity, phaseTag, and NPC anchor, and the `post-stairs` unlocked-stair suppression exception is preserved. Scope is well-contained; validation is loud and covered by targeted failure tests, and the module-load `validateScenarioAiTaskConfig` against the compiled quest registry protects the canonical-quest linkage. Determinism is preserved (pure functions; no clocks/RNG). Test coverage of the generic interpreter is strong via `tests/game/scenario-ai-tasks.test.ts`; Floor 1's byte-equivalence is asserted only indirectly through the existing headless tests referenced in the handoff (no new Floor-1-specific snapshot fixtures), which is the one place a targeted regression test would harden the claim — enough to keep test_coverage below 5 but not a blocker.
